items.prompt: Can DSU parent pointers be used as the original shortest graph path?

options.text: Yes, because each parent is necessarily the last input edge
options.why: Union attaches roots, not necessarily the input edge endpoints.

options.text: Yes, because representatives encode hop distances
options.why: Representative IDs do not encode distance.

options.text: No, because undirected graphs can never have paths
options.why: Undirected graphs can have paths; DSU does not store the required route.

options.text: No; the forest represents connectivity, not original routes
options.why: Keep original adjacency and a path algorithm when routes matter.

items.explanation: A connectivity representation and a path witness are different data products. Do not infer original edges from DSU attachment links.
